newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah little changed in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah little changed in sluggish trade.

text.p: Indonesia's rupiah was little changed against the dollar in sluggish late trading on Tuesday ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve policy meeting, dealers said.

One major local bank dealer said trading was pretty quiet, with operators reluctant to take the initiative due to the month-end factor and the U.S. Federal Open Market Committe (FOMC) meeting later on Tuesday.
"The market has been really dull in the past two days. I don't expect much at present," the dealer said.
He said operators' focus now was on liquidity, which was seen as much more important than the U.S. interest rates.
"If the Federal Reserve hikes rates by 0.25 percentage point, there won't be much effect on the market. The main issue for us now is liquidity," the dealer said.
But one U.S. bank dealer said earlier there could be some portfolio adjustments if it were a 0.5 percentage point raise.
Dealers said the market seemed to have factored in a 0.25 percentage point rise in interest rates by the Federal Reserve.

Spot rupiah was last at 2,318.25/18.75 at 0900 GMT against an opening of 2,318.5/19.5. One Japanese bank dealer said some short-covering of dollars was seen late in the afternoon but strong support for the rupiah persisted.
"There was no change in sentiment on the rupiah. It would still be traded around the ceiling," one said.
He expected the dollar-rupiah rate to range between 2,318.0 and 2,320.0 on Wednesday. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,317.70/18.00 and 2,317.75/18.00, respectively.

The Japanese bank dealer said overnight money was last traded at 9.5 percent, with a stable outlook seen for Wednesday as Tuesday's excess supply was placed in overnight papers (SBIs) offered by the central bank at nine percent.
"I'm not so worried about liquidity supply until Thursday but people are worrying over a possible repeat of tight conditions on Friday," the dealer said.
Jakarta's interbank market was hit by tight rupiah supply in the last two Fridays, causing operators to cash in one-week papers for temporary liquidity, but with a carry-forward effect.
Some dealers said the impact might have subsided but banks remained cautious due to the month-end factor.
Overnight swap was at 0.25/0.35. Tom/next swap rate eased to 0.45/0.50 from 0.52/0.55 points on ample liquidity.
Dealers said longer-term swap rates were stable.
They said earlier players seemed to make some deals in anticipation of the FOMC meeting, with light unloading of swaps due to worries over narrowing interest rates differentials.
"If the FOMC meeting hikes short-term rates, the immediate impact could be felt on the swap rate because of the narrowing interest rate gap between the two currencies," one said.
One-month swap was last at 15.50/16.25, two at 30.50/31.25, three at 46.25/47.00 and six at 95.50/96.00 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention rate at 2,313/2,505 and the conversion rate at 2,313/2,361 on Tuesday.
